vulnerability_class: CWE-184 (Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs) -> CWE-78 (OS Command Injection)
description: GitPython blocks dangerous git options like --upload-pack, --receive-pack, --exec, -u, -c, and --config by checking raw kwarg names in Git.check_unsafe_options(). But Git.transform_kwarg() later 'dashifies' underscore-form kwargs (upload_pack -> --upload-pack) when building the actual command line. Because check_unsafe_options() runs on the pre-dashified kwarg names, an underscore-spelled kwarg such as upload_pack (the normal, idiomatic Python spelling) sails through the check and is still turned into --upload-pack on the command line, invoking an attacker-controlled helper program during clone/fetch/pull/push -- even with the documented default allow_unsafe_options=False protection in place. The literal hyphenated spelling `{'upload-pack': ...}` is correctly blocked; only the underscore spelling is missed.

vulnerable_call_sites.role: checks list(kwargs.keys()) against clone's unsafe-option list before the kwargs are dashified
same pattern -- checks raw kwargs.keys() before dashification
root cause: does substring/exact matching against un-normalized option names, so 'upload_pack' != 'upload-pack' never triggers the block
the later, unrelated step that converts upload_pack -> --upload-pack -- this is where the bypassed value actually becomes the dangerous CLI flag

fix_approach: Canonicalize both the configured unsafe-option names and the incoming option/kwarg names through the same normalization (dashify + strip leading dashes + drop any '=value' suffix) before comparing, so 'upload_pack' and '--upload-pack' and 'upload-pack' are all recognized as the same option. GitPython's real fix added Git._canonicalize_option_name() and rewrote check_unsafe_options() to build a dict keyed by the canonical form and look up each incoming option by its canonical form.
notes: This is a logic/timing gap, not a missing-sanitization bug: the safety check exists and is invoked, but it operates on data before a later normalization step changes its meaning. The fix must not simply add 'upload_pack' as another blocked literal (that would still miss e.g. -uVALUE or other forms) -- it needs to normalize consistently.
poc_source: Adapted from the advisory's PoC: git/cmd.py's check_unsafe_options blocks {'upload-pack': helper} but Remote.fetch(upload_pack=helper) reaches and executes the helper program.
